title: ETH AI Center Researchers Community Meetup
venue: ETH AI Center, OAT X 11, Oerlikon
blurb: Recurring meetup series for the AI research community at ETH Zurich.

title: Les Rendez-vous de la HEG-Genève : De l’IA aux résultats
venue: HEG-Genève, Campus Battelle, Rue de la Tambourine 17
organiser: HEG-Genève / Observatoire Data & IA (with Oracle and Colombus Consulting)
blurb: Round table in which four organisations present AI initiatives that moved past the pilot stage to measurable business impact — the organisers promise fewer speeches and more lived experience — followed by a cocktail.

title: UNIGE – Recherche documentaire et IA
blurb: University of Geneva workshop on using AI tools for academic research.

title: Women & AI: How to Lead Change & Build the Future
organiser: Startup Campus (on behalf of Innosuisse) with Female Founders Initiative Switzerland
blurb: Zurich founders and AI practitioners on how they actually use AI inside their companies and lead teams through the change it brings, followed by an open panel and networking.

title: The Judgements You Cannot Outsource
organiser: Trustworthy AI Circle (Responsible AI Innovation Group, ZHAW)
blurb: Short talks and open discussion on which professional judgements should stay human as AI absorbs more decisions, with Chuck Garcia (Columbia Engineering), Pascal Wiscour-Conter and Dr Jacqueline Kucera (IDHEAP, UNIL).

title: Knowledge Transfer in the Age of AI
organiser: ETH Student Project House with Prometheus, UZH.ai and Young AI Leaders Zurich
blurb: A workshop plus panel on how AI changes knowledge transfer between research, industry and new talent, with ETH Zurich, Artefact and KPMG Switzerland’s head of AI answering questions the room drafts first.

title: Aipéro
blurb: A German-language evening of drinks, snacks and expert interviews in Zurich, built around the launch of the first issue of ZAITUNG — a paper written by AI journalists from the community’s own answers on what a human in the loop needs to know.

title: Agentic Trio
blurb: INNOQ’s Fabian Walther reframes Teresa Torres’ Product Trio as an "Agentic Trio", arguing that AI should change how software teams split responsibility — not just how fast they ship.

title: AI in Food — State of Play
organiser: Swiss Food & Nutrition Valley / Porsche Consulting
blurb: A full day of keynotes and workshops for food-industry professionals past the AI hype stage, on what it actually takes to implement AI against real problems inside their own organisations.

title: AI Swiss x Groupe Mutuel : d’une discussion d’équipe à une IA façonnée pour elle, avec BASE
blurb: Second stop of AI Swiss’s roadshow on BASE, its free open standard for responsible AI adoption, with a live demonstration turning a transcribed team interview into an agreed usage framework, plus a Q&A on limits and oversight.

title: Apertus for NGOs: Running and Deploying Switzerland’s Open-source LLM
organiser: Swiss AI Initiative (ETH Zurich, EPFL & CSCS)
blurb: Hands-on morning for non-profit staff and researchers on deploying Apertus, Switzerland’s fully open large language model, on their own infrastructure or via a provider — with a Swiss non-profit case study and group exercises.

title: C4DT Conference on AI Sovereignty: Charting Switzerland’s Path
blurb: A full day on how Switzerland builds strategic independence in AI between US and Chinese dominance — lessons from other middle powers, Swiss research including the Apertus foundation model, industry deployment realities, and concrete recommendations for national strategy.

title: Navigating Data Protection and Transfer Impact Assessments for AI Startups
blurb: Breakfast session with lawyers from Wenger Vieli on when a Transfer Impact Assessment is actually required for cross-border data transfers, and how to keep them manageable as an AI company.

title: DevOps for Fabric — Git & Deployment Pipelines
organiser: Data and AI for Intelligent Cloud
blurb: Bringing proper CI/CD to Microsoft Fabric: Git integration, deployment pipelines, variable libraries and sensitivity labels for enterprise-ready BI.

title: Machine Intelligence Summit
cost: Not listed (curated attendance, host approval required)
blurb: Three hundred people who build frontier AI in Europe, across four 80-minute blocks — infrastructure, learning, agents and the physical world — each pairing academia, a frontier lab and a startup, plus founder lightning talks and fifty students presenting posters. Nothing is recorded.

title: MUG Zürich — How to Truly Stop AI Hallucinations
blurb: Two talks from Helvetia Insurance engineers: why factual errors in generative AI apps usually come from weak retrieval design rather than the model — covering semantic chunking, metadata filtering, hybrid search, reranking and output guardrails — and a second session on the benefits and risks of AI-assisted development.

title: Rethinking Architecture Through Residuality and AI
organiser: Software Architecture and Project Design Zurich
blurb: Barry O’Reilly’s Residuality Theory applied to the age of AI-generated code: what architects should still decide themselves when machines write the implementation. Live stream plus a few on-site seats at ERNI.

title: aiHealth 2026 — 3rd International Annual Conference on Artificial Intelligence in Health
organiser: FHNW School of Life Sciences with Bioevents
blurb: A two-morning boutique conference bringing clinicians, industry and academics together across three sessions — AI for diagnostics, AI for therapeutics and AI in citizen health.

title: Learning Lunch : alternatives numériques — quelles options et quels impacts pour les PME ?
cost: Not listed (reserved for companies based in the canton of Neuchâtel; registration by email)
blurb: A French-language lunch session on alternatives to the large technology providers — digital commons, open-source platforms and decentralised infrastructure — with Lionel Jeannerat on the open-source sales platform be-BOP and Fabio Bonfiglio of NEDAO on decentralised identity and AI.

title: AI Safety Weekly: Steering Vectors & Input Optimisation
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, room HG D3.3
blurb: A bachelor’s thesis presentation on automatically optimising a prompt to reproduce the effect of a steering vector, and whether such an input still works on models you cannot inspect from the inside — followed by wider interpretability discussion and food.

title: AI-Stammtisch | St.Gallen
venue: OST Campus St.Gallen, Raum FZ.0132 (FHZ), Rosenbergstrasse 59
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (Institut für Informations- und Prozessmanagement)
blurb: The monthly Eastern Switzerland AI round table, this time on whether a model may write the tests for safety-critical software — how far generated results can be trusted and how quality is kept — drawing on the Innosuisse project “Functional Safety Agent”. Followed by an apéro; the talk can also be followed online.

title: Inside ETH Zurich’s Data Stack: Analytics for Universities
blurb: A walk through a real analytics stack built with ETH Zurich — the original setup and why, what got bolted on later, how individual departments were brought up to speed with the data, and where it goes next — then open discussion over drinks.

title: east#KI 2026
organiser: IT rockt! (ICT Cluster Ostschweiz) with swissAI
blurb: Second edition of Eastern Switzerland’s AI evening: a panel on how safe AI really is, five-minute pitches from regional companies, an AI table fair and a networking apéro.

title: IKM Impuls: Vom Trigger zum Agenten
organiser: HSLU Institut für Kommunikation und Marketing (IKM)
blurb: Lunchtime session from HSLU on what changes when marketing automation stops following rules and starts deciding, and what companies need in data, technology and organisation to run AI agents in customer dialogue.

title: OpenTech Connect 2026 — Day 1: INSPIRE
organiser: Data, Cloud and AI in Switzerland (with Big Data University and IBM Research)
blurb: First day of a two-day open-technology gathering at EPFL Innovation Park, with talks, demos, lightning sessions and panel discussions on data, AI and open technology for researchers, students, developers and industry.

title: SPRINT Robotics Europe Summit 2026
cost: EUR 400 community / EUR 900 non-members / EUR 150 students
blurb: Two-day European summit on robotics, AI and autonomous technology for industrial inspection, maintenance and operations, hosted at ETH Zürich, with company visits on the second day.

title: Swiss AI Industry Connect
organiser: EPFL & ETH Zurich, hosted by Swisscom
blurb: Half-day morning session at Swisscom’s Bern office bringing EPFL and ETH Zurich AI researchers together with industry partners.

title: Swiss Data & AI — AI Enabled Workflows
organiser: Swiss Data and AI Group (Databricks User Group)
blurb: The first Zurich gathering of the Swiss Data & AI group, on automating data work with AI-enabled workflows. Topics, speakers and the venue are still to be announced, and the group is open to offers to speak.

title: The Robotics Founder’s Guide: Find Your Ideal Customer with Data
venue: ETH AI Center, Andreasstrasse 5, OAT X11, Oerlikon
organiser: ETH AI Center with Vantastics, Nebius and Limbi
blurb: A hands-on session for robotics and deep-tech teams on choosing a first market: comparing customer segments, testing assumptions against market and sales data, and using AI to spot buying signals. Networking drinks follow.

title: AI Startup Center Community Meetup — November Edition
blurb: A deliberately informal morning meetup over coffee for the centre’s AI startups and corporate partners — no agenda and no presentations, just conversations about partnerships, where AI is heading and what is actually hard right now.

title: Business Leaders' Evening: Your AI, your data, under your roof
venue: LeBooster Genève, Route de Jussy 35 (2nd floor)
organiser: ABAXINFO / AXION / Keeping Life Simple, hosted by CCI France Suisse
blurb: A French-language evening for SME leaders on getting value from AI without giving up control of the data: three levels of sovereign AI, a live demo of a fully offline model answering on a sample company’s documents with per-employee permissions, what the revised Swiss data protection act expects of management, and a networking apéro.

title: Why Adam Works in Optimizing Language Models: Heavy-Tailed Data Imbalance
venue: ETH AI Center, OAT X 11, Andreasstrasse 5, Oerlikon
blurb: Frederik Kunstner (INRIA) on why plain gradient descent struggles to train language models while Adam does not — tracing the gap to Zipf-law imbalance in language data, with empirical results and a proof on a linear bigram model.

title: IA : meetup « Generative AI Genève » #5
blurb: Your data, your models, your infrastructure: ELCA and EPFL spin-off Anyway Systems on running LLMs locally or in a private cloud, and on the trade-offs between performance, sovereignty and cost when a company wants generative AI without handing over its data.

title: OpenTech Connect 2026 — Day 2: BUILD
organiser: Data, Cloud and AI in Switzerland (with Big Data University and IBM Research)
blurb: Hands-on second day of OpenTech Connect: workshops, technical deep dives and practical labs with speakers from LlamaIndex, Skilder, Synergix and IBM Research. Registration is separate from day one.

title: SC71: Meetup Database / PostgreSQL
venue: Swissquote Bank SA, Chemin de la Crétaux 33
blurb: Two database talks hosted by Swissquote in Gland — PostgreSQL on Kubernetes with Laurent Parodi and multi-version concurrency control with Louis Tochon — followed by a quiz and apéro.

title: AI Futures: Trajectories for a Post-AGI Civilization
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, Room F 26.5
blurb: Part of a discussion series on where AI development leads: expert forecasts for transformative AI, the economic effects of AGI, possible civilisational paths and what to do about them, mixing short explainers with group discussion.

title: Smart-Energy App mit KI entwickeln
blurb: A hands-on German-language evening building your own smart-meter app with opencode.ai or Claude Code: pulling Swiss spot prices from the BKW API, logging feed-in readings hourly and writing monthly compensation out to CSV. Bring a laptop, a gPlug and Docker.

title: ETH AI Club DEMO NIGHT #2
blurb: Five minutes live, no slides: ETH AI Club members demo AI side projects they built for fun or to fix a real problem, then take questions and keep talking over apéro at Swisscom Ventures.

title: Effizienter Arbeiten mit KI-Tools wie ChatGPT: Prompting für die öffentliche Verwaltung
blurb: A German-language day course for public-administration staff on getting useful work out of tools like ChatGPT — prompting technique, where the tools fail, and what to watch for with official data. Currently sold out.

title: Swiss Robotics Day 2026
organiser: ETH Zurich RobotX / Swiss Robotics Association
blurb: The national robotics meeting point: keynotes, panels and workshops alongside an exhibition floor with 60+ exhibitors and live demos, bringing together labs, industry, policymakers and spin-offs.

title: Mit Claude in die Agentic Economy
blurb: A four-hour German-language workshop for non-programmers in management roles: build your own tool with Claude Code, then cover Skills and Projects for reuse plus data protection and model choice. Five to ten participants.

title: Seminar «Mein erster Finance Agent – Praxisworkshop für KMU»
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (IFL Institut für Finance und Law)
blurb: A German-language day for SME finance leads with no programming background: each participant builds an agent on their own laptop that prepares a monthly close from Excel data, summarises liquidity trends and works through debtor lists, with output to PDF or Excel.

title: Energ-IACK — Hackathon IA & énergie
blurb: First edition of Geneva’s two-day AI and energy hackathon on the theme « Dessine-moi un NetZéro », where teams work on energy-transition challenges; the projects then present their results at the energIA conference on 1 December.

title: Coffee & Prompt #011
blurb: The Geneva builders’ weekend coworking morning: bring an AI project or side hustle, work alongside others, and optionally show a feature or a lesson learned for feedback from the room.

title: Hype vs. Shipped: What AI Really Changes in Product Work
blurb: Two talks on what AI has actually changed in building products: Coople on a year spent replacing squads, sprints and story points with AI-first workflows and smaller teams, including the experiments that failed, and Brack.Alltron on where AI earned its place and why plain analytics sometimes still beats machine learning.

title: Swiss AI Summit 2026
cost: CHF 790 Executive Pass / CHF 950 standard (excl. VAT)
blurb: Full-day summit at the Kunsthaus for senior business, technology and government leaders, spanning finance and insurance, government and defence, manufacturing, cybersecurity, quantum and healthcare — with speakers from Microsoft Switzerland, IBM, Nestlé, ABB, HSBC and the Canton of Zurich, plus workshops, demos and a one-to-one meeting platform.

title: AI in azienda: AI sotto controllo
venue: Campus Est USI-SUPSI, Blocco C, Aula C1.02, Via la Santa 1, Viganello
blurb: Closing evening of the Ticino series on conscious AI use in business, this one on data, responsibility, rules and governance — content, a hands-on workshop and networking, capped at thirty participants.

title: Cloud Native Computing Meetup — November 2026
blurb: Three talks and an apéro: the guardrails Open Systems put in place before letting an AI agent work on its Kubernetes clusters, a Rust-based zero-dependency etcd replacement with the QuantyKube sandbox, and a session on Jellyfin.

title: Building a Multi-AZ Cloud in Switzerland & Embedding Quality in Agile Delivery
blurb: The group’s last evening of 2026: Hidora on building a highly available multi-availability-zone cloud in Switzerland on Kubernetes, and a talk on defining quality processes across several teams in scrum-of-scrums delivery.

title: Boosting Life Sciences Innovation with AI
blurb: Lunchtime session with the Wyss Center AI Hub, SOPHiA GENETICS, the Swiss Data Science Center and BrainQuant on the data, infrastructure, validation and regulatory groundwork behind AI in research partnerships, precision medicine and digital biomarkers.

title: Growing Together Conference GTC26
venue: The Circle Convention Center, The Circle 27
blurb: A full day for business and data leaders on getting AI past isolated use cases and into scalable capability — keynotes from Benedict Evans and Google Cloud’s Alon Halevy, leader tracks with Helvetia, Axpo and Emmi, plus tech talks and workshops.

title: AI in Production: Introduction to MLOps — Training at EPFL
cost: CHF 1,000 (10% off for EPFL alumni and SDSC partners)
blurb: One-day SDSC training on designing, deploying and operating ML systems at scale — version control, CI/CD, experiment tracking, monitoring, drift detection and automated retraining. Registration closes 24 September.

title: Satellite Event: From Data to Decisions — AI in Asset Management
blurb: A Swiss AI Summit satellite session on how asset managers turn increasingly complex data into usable investment insight, and where AI makes a genuine difference rather than noise.

title: Satellite Event: From Smart AI to Better Work
blurb: An interactive executive lab run with Zeix on redesigning work around AI: deciding what the machine should actually do, and marking out where human judgement, responsibility and control have to stay.

title: The Glass Box Roadshow — Executive Track Zurich
blurb: An evening counterpart to the roadshow for leaders accountable for AI returns: a keynote from someone who has already rolled AI out in their company, a live demonstration and a closed-door roundtable.

title: The Glass Box Roadshow — Zurich
blurb: Make’s Zurich stop on where AI automation already works and where it does not: live demos, a product roadmap session, an open panel and lunch, aimed at operations, IT and transformation leads scaling automation across teams.

title: SAIC #041: AI in Healthcare & Pharma — From Breakthrough Technology to Better Patient Outcomes
venue: Maison Internationale des Associations, Rue des Savoises 15
cost: CHF 5 in person (50 places) / free online livestream
blurb: Dr Stamen Popov on where AI already adds value from drug discovery to patient support, and where trust, ethics, regulation and adoption still get in the way of better outcomes.

title: AI Safety Weekly: Alignment from Token Zero
venue: ETH Main Building, HG D3.3, Rämistrasse 101
blurb: V. Moskvoretskii (EPFL) on building an assistant persona into pretraining rather than bolting alignment on afterwards — a technique now part of training Apertus 2, Switzerland’s open model. Moderate technical background assumed.

title: Applied AI Journal Club Bern #10
blurb: Monthly reading group in Bern where the group works through one applied-AI article together, with time afterwards for open exchange; the paper is shared in advance.

title: Digital Series #13 — Moins d’administratif grâce à l’IA
venue: Co-working La Bergerie, Place du Midi 50
organiser: Swiss Digital Center / Fondation The Ark (with CCI Valais)
blurb: Valais SMEs see how AI agents can take over routine admin — client requests, bookings, contracts and follow-up — with a live tool demo and a local case study from the Sion coworking space.

title: Sovereign AI Night by Giotto
blurb: Launch evening for Giotto Alto and Solo: meet the team, try the models, watch a Giotto Workstation demo and argue about what sovereignty in AI actually requires — with pizza, drinks and live music.

title: AWS Swiss User Group Geneva #30: Kiro Nights
blurb: A beginner-friendly hands-on evening building a working web app from scratch with Kiro, AWS's agentic IDE, with the organisers on hand to help — bring a laptop, pizza and apéro included.

title: AI Observability Switzerland — Giving Your AI Systems the Visibility They Deserve
organiser: Swiss Digital Network (Effective SRE & DevOps Community) with Grafana Labs
blurb: An hour for engineering, platform and data teams on tracking down rising token costs, stuck agent chains and slower model responses — monitoring LLM calls without custom instrumentation, tracing agent chains with OpenTelemetry, and setting up continuous evaluation to catch quality drops.

title: DINAcon 2026
blurb: Switzerland’s conference on digital sustainability — 36 sessions on open source, open data, digital sovereignty, data protection and copyright, with 250+ attendees and a closing Hacknight.

title: Agentic Nights #1 — Identity, Software Factories & Agent Memory
blurb: First evening of Global AI Zürich’s new agentic series, with three talks on real agent implementations covering identity, software factories and agent memory.

title: Brown Bag: Copilot erfolgreich einführen — KI-Power im Büroalltag
organiser: InnovationsBiotop Uri with Business Help Point
cost: Free (optional lunch CHF 9; registration by 16 November)
blurb: A German-language lunch hour on the organisational side of Microsoft 365 Copilot rather than prompt tricks: Roman Schön on why AI initiatives stall, why structure and context beat perfectly worded prompts, and what it takes to make the tool stick in day-to-day office work.

title: The 4th Innovation Debate: AI for All?
venue: Westhive, Bâtiment Alto, Esplanade de Pont-Rouge 9A
organiser: Geneva Innovation Movement and Geneva Research Lab for Digital Impact, with UNICEF Digital Impact Division and the University of Geneva
blurb: An Oxford-style debate on the motion “access to AI is worth the dependency it creates”, with four debaters, a jury of Geneva politicians and an audience vote, followed by a networking apéritif.

title: AI Risks in CyberSecurity
venue: Novotel Genève Centre, Rue de Zurich 19
blurb: Afternoon session in Geneva on how organisations can keep using AI internally without taking on unmanaged risk, with presentations followed by a networking reception; CPE credits available via ISC2 and ISACA.

title: Digital Economy Award 2026
organiser: Swiss Digital Economy Award AG with digitalswitzerland
blurb: Switzerland’s digital-economy awards at the Hallenstadion: an Executive Afternoon of nine partner-hosted sessions on AI, customer relationships, skills and stablecoins, followed by the Award Night for categories from Pioneer of the Year to NextGen Hero.

title: Conférence Next — Design x IA
venue: QG Center, Route de la Chaux 4 (QoQa)
blurb: An afternoon on what AI has actually changed in design work: a study of how 100 designers use it, prototyping with AI agents directly against a codebase, and how Swissquote rebuilt its design system with AI — then networking drinks.

title: AI Safety: Open Meet Up
cost: Free (registration required, food and drinks provided)
blurb: An evening with no fixed programme in place of the usual weekly session: meet the organisers, ask how the AI safety field is put together, or pick up a thread from an earlier talk — newcomers as welcome as people already working on it.

title: Agentic Engineering Days Zurich 2026
blurb: A one-day engineering conference on AI coding and agent systems: 38+ sessions across four tracks — using AI tools, building AI-powered systems, sponsor spotlights and hands-on workshops — with speakers from OpenAI, Hugging Face, NVIDIA, Google and AWS.

title: AI Breakfast #56 Luzern
blurb: Merun Gugelmann of Aeberli Treuhand on how an 80-year-old trust company got from Microsoft Teams to building its own Azure applications — the steps of that digitisation journey, concrete examples, and the setup on Azure App Services.

title: AI Society — AI Coffee Chats Zurich (20 November)
blurb: Fortnightly drop-in coffee hour for anyone working with AI in Zurich: no presentations, just questions, demos and shop talk over an hour.

title: Data Science Final Project Presentations
blurb: Open evening where data science students present their end-to-end projects, from data collection and analysis through modelling to visualisation, followed by questions and networking.

title: STEM4Health Hackathon
venue: ETH Zürich Campus Hönggerberg, HPH building
organiser: Johnson & Johnson Switzerland / Swiss Data Science Center
blurb: A hundred students and early-career researchers spend a weekend on real pharmaceutical manufacturing problems, combining manufacturing data, mechanistic modelling and machine learning with industry and academic mentors before pitching to a jury.

title: Basel AI & Vibe Coding Club — First Meetup
blurb: Kick-off meetup for a new Basel group around AI-assisted coding: short intros, side-project show-and-tell, and an open round on what people want to build next.

title: Basel Data Science & AI Meetup — November 2026
blurb: Three practical talks on getting machine learning and AI models deployed and running in production, followed by networking with the Basel data community.

title: AI Tinkerers Lausanne — November 2026 Meetup
organiser: AI Tinkerers Lausanne, hosted at the Unlimitrust Campus
blurb: A demo-first evening for people actually building with AI: around half a dozen five-minute demos of work in progress, each followed by questions — slides and pitch decks are explicitly not allowed — then pizza and networking.

title: AI Safety: Building Trustworthy AI in the Real World
organiser: Elevate Tech: Women and Minorities in AI, Tech, and Science
blurb: Four speakers from Google, AWS, Unique and Systematic-X on keeping AI systems trustworthy once they act on their own — how to evaluate and monitor before and after deployment, where guardrails, human oversight and red-teaming fit, and how to ship fast without losing accountability.

title: Apertus Claritas: An Inside View of Switzerland’s Open Model
venue: ETH AI Center Foyer, OAT X 11, Andreasstrasse 5, Oerlikon
blurb: Lightning talks from the interpretability and safety hub built around Apertus, Switzerland’s open multilingual model: shared representations across languages, emergent misalignment from stereotypes that pass moderation, probes that catch repetition loops early, and persona binding formed in pre-training.

title: KI-Agenten & -Work: Skills und Anbindungen für konkrete Entlastung im Alltag
blurb: A full German-language day with Michael Kyburz on getting AI to take over recurring work: three base skills, how to build your own, and wiring assistants into calendar, mail and project tools so multi-step workflows run with clear checkpoints for human review. Fifteen places, and a paid ChatGPT or Claude subscription is required.

title: Built with Lovable · Lausanne #2
cost: Free (host approval required; Lovable credits included)
blurb: A 90-minute hands-on build where everyone ships a working web app with AI features using Lovable’s built-in models — no API keys or separate accounts — with mentors on hand, then demos and drinks. Bring a laptop and an idea.

title: AI Safety Weekly: Finding Your Way Into AI Safety
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, room HG D3.3
blurb: A map of the routes into AI safety and governance work — fellowships, research programmes, who is eligible, when they open and how they are funded — with people who have been through them answering questions. No particular background needed.

title: The Geneva AI Conference 2026
blurb: An evening on enterprise AI strategy and returns, opened by Geneva city executive councillor Joëlle Bertossa and built around a panel with IBM, SAP, Hostelworld and Executive AI. The venue is still to be confirmed.

title: Kongress «KI im Energiesektor»
blurb: Day-long congress bringing around 150 specialists from energy, technology and policy together on where AI and data create real value in grids, buildings and districts, with a keynote by Gerard Reid of Alexa Capital.

title: Mindstone Geneva November AI Meetup
venue: L’Annexe by Rentes Genevoises, Rue du Port 3
blurb: Monthly Geneva AI evening with three practical talks — building with LLMs, working faster with AI and where it is all heading — then pizza and networking. Forty places.

title: Zurich Pre-NeurIPS 2026 Poster Session
venue: ETH AI Center, OAT X 11, Oerlikon
organiser: ETH AI Center / Zurich ELLIS Unit
blurb: Zurich’s official pre-conference poster session ahead of NeurIPS 2026, where researchers from across the city show accepted papers and other peer-reviewed work and meet the rest of the local AI community.

title: DemystifAI 01 — Homebrewed
venue: Maison de la Femme, Avenue de l’Eglantine 6
blurb: Kouros, who is not a developer and has a full-time job, explains how he used AI to build a custom ERP for the La Nébuleuse brewery, followed by guided discussion, audience questions and an apéro.

title: Visualizing Peace Indicators by Interactive Things
blurb: Designers and developers from Interactive Things walk through how they turned qualitative peace indicators from around the world into a comparable visual dataset.

title: L’impresa potenziata con AI
blurb: An Italian-language afternoon in Chiasso built on real cases and measured numbers rather than promises: AI agents in the business, sovereign data, and what institutions are for — closing with a networking apéro.

title: Real or Generated? | SAIC x The Founders Club
organiser: Switzerland AI Community with The Founders Club
blurb: Playful challenges to tell real images, sounds and text apart from AI-generated ones, with curated visuals, music and networking across Geneva's tech, creative and founder communities.

title: Bessere Ergebnisse mit generativer KI: Advanced Prompting für die öffentliche Verwaltung
blurb: A German-language follow-on course for public-sector staff who already use generative AI daily: controlling output more precisely, building reusable prompt templates, and setting up your own CustomGPT or Copilot agent against your own use cases.

title: Robot Learning Paper Club — The World Model Edition
blurb: Short talks and paper walkthroughs on learned world models for robotics — action-conditioned video prediction, joint observation and action models, planning and policy evaluation, and synthetic data generation.

title: Writing The Living Organization — What AI Is Doing to How We Organize
blurb: Breeze Dong on the operating model behind her book The Living Organization, and an open discussion of what happens to teams, roles and decision-making when AI agents join the work.

title: Chalet Azure Romandie #17 — Talents Microsoft & Azure Local
blurb: A French-language Azure evening in Geneva: what AI has really changed about Microsoft recruitment and how candidates stay visible, then Azure Local for running Azure services inside a sovereign private cloud, with a live Foundry Local demo — quiz and networking afterwards.

title: HSG Fintech Summit 2026
cost: Not listed (separate ticket categories for HSG alumni, faculty and students)
blurb: The University of St.Gallen’s fintech day, themed this year on what AI does to finance: keynotes on AI in financial intermediation and asset management, research talks on model collapse, AI errors and moral hazard, a panel on AI’s effect on markets, and a closing apéro.

title: AI Futures: What's the Plan?
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, Room F 26.5
blurb: Fourth session of the AI Futures series, turning from the risks to the responses: technical safety work such as alignment, control, interpretability and evaluations; governance and policy including compute rules and treaties; and socio-structural preparedness — with the organisers’ own read on what looks most promising.

title: Cloud Native Bern Meetup — November 2026
blurb: Two talks and an apéro hosted by Puzzle: wiring Amazon RDS to TimescaleDB with foreign data wrappers for federated Postgres on EKS — and where 10 TB starts to break it — then PostFinance on moving cloud and AI cost awareness earlier, and what AI cost governance takes.

title: After Microsoft Ignite Special 2026
organiser: Swiss Microsoft Community (Microsoft Cloud Security & Modern Work)
blurb: Swiss MVPs recap the announcements from Microsoft Ignite 2026 in short sessions on Cloud & AI, the agent platform, Copilot and Microsoft IQ, security, data security and compliance, and agentic business applications, with an apéro after.

title: Hack Apertus — Onsite Hackathon Zurich
blurb: The on-site leg of the national Apertus hackathon: build on the open Apertus 8B model, strengthen its multilingual abilities and ship applications for private- and public-sector problems, with everything released as Open Commons.

title: AI Insights for Chief Executives
venue: Swiss AI Tower, ETH Zürich, Andreasstrasse 5
blurb: Executive workshop for CEOs, CFOs, CDOs and CTOs on turning data and AI into measurable business value, with case studies from EKZ, Merck and Richemont. Limited seats.

title: AI Agent Sandbox: Bring Your Ideas, Let's Explore Together!
blurb: An in-person working session where the group picks one AI agent idea from the room and explores it together with sticky notes, sketches and a timer — open to beginners and active builders alike.

title: Azure Zurich AI Infrastructure Night
blurb: In-person evening at Digicomp on the infrastructure side of running AI workloads on Azure.

title: AI for Business: Network, Learn & Grow in Zurich
venue: ibis Styles Zurich City Center, Stampfenbachstrasse 60
cost: Ticket required via Eventfrog (some early-bird tickets free; drinks not included)
blurb: A deliberately small room of founders and executives comparing how they actually use AI: an invited talk, then group conversations on what worked, what failed and what they are trying next, followed by open networking.

title: Databricks Executive Roundtable — Data + AI World Tour Zurich
cost: Not listed (Executive Program pass, apply to attend)
blurb: An invitation-based dinner and discussion for data and technology executives the evening before the Data + AI World Tour, with a welcome from Databricks leadership and a Swiss customer segment; sessions and speakers are still to be announced.

title: AIristoteles 4.0 — Bis dass der Strom uns scheidet
organiser: HSLU Institut für Kommunikation und Marketing (IKM)
blurb: Fourth edition of HSLU’s AIristoteles series: an EPFL evolutionary psychologist and a psychotherapist discuss what it means when people enter long-term relationships with AI bots, moderated by Stephan Klapproth and followed by an apéro.

title: Databricks Data + AI World Tour Zurich 2026
blurb: Databricks' flagship Swiss stop on the Data + AI World Tour: keynotes, breakout sessions and hands-on training on Genie and Lakebase, plus an expo, with speakers from Databricks and Zurich Insurance.

title: Reshaping Information Research with AI
blurb: Two-hour on-site workshop from the EPFL Library comparing four AI-powered research assistants, how they work and where they differ from traditional information retrieval. Open to the public, registration required.

title: IBM Bob Coding Watch Party Zürich — Final Edition
blurb: The closing session of IBM's 2026 hybrid series on IBM Bob, its AI development assistant — coding live alongside other European cities, with beginner, intermediate and expert tracks covering everything from first idea to modernising legacy applications.

title: KI-Strategie und -Governance für KMUs
blurb: A 90-minute German-language session for SME decision-makers on steering generative AI use rather than letting it spread: setting a strategic frame, drafting an internal AI policy, weighing data-protection, liability and wrong-output risks, and planning a safe rollout under Swiss data protection law and the EU AI Act. Fifteen places.

title: TechTalk #30 @ Nine — What Tools Won’t Do for You
blurb: Build-and-deploy evening at Nine: nxt Engineering on how not to wreck an Azure migration, and Access for all on why manual accessibility testing still matters alongside automated and AI-assisted checks. Also livestreamed.

title: AWS Swiss User Group Bern — December Meetup
blurb: Final Bern meetup of the year for the Swiss AWS community: a mix of community talks plus discussion and networking, with the agenda announced closer to the date.

title: energIA 2026 — IA & décarbonation
blurb: Second edition of the Geneva conference on AI and the energy transition, debating whether AI genuinely helps reach net zero by 2050 or mostly adds resource consumption and rebound effects, with public, private and academic participants and the Energ-IACK hackathon projects presenting their results.

title: Ein Team, ein Plan und viele Agenten
blurb: A German-language breakfast session with Quatico CEO Jan Wloka on why adding more AI agents tends to produce more review work than finished work, and the three changes that fixed it for his team: a written decision before any agent starts coding, work split into packages that run in parallel, and one daily overview of what needs a human. Aimed at product owners and delivery leads, with a real work package run live.

title: KI-Update x swissAI Meetup — Die Auswirkungen der KI auf Kinder
blurb: Free German-language evening in Gebenstorf: a current AI update from Michael Kyburz, then Alexander Repenning on what AI means for children, closing with an apéro with the swissAI community.

title: Swiss IT Minds 2026 — IT, AI & Cyber Security
cost: Not listed (complimentary participation for qualified attendees)
blurb: Two days for Swiss IT and data leaders at the Dolder Grand on enterprise AI as a strategic capability, centralised versus decentralised AI governance in large organisations, securing AI agents as a hybrid workforce, and the governance basics behind all of it.

title: Robotics Garage Night
blurb: Show-and-tell evening for people building robots: short demos of works in progress, honest accounts of what broke, then food and conversation.

title: 40 ans d’informatique en Valais — Conférence #3 : l’ERP, colonne vertébrale de l’entreprise, à l’ère de l’IA
venue: Campus Bellevue, Rte de la Plaine 2
organiser: HES-SO Valais-Wallis (Haute École de Gestion & Tourisme, filière Informatique de gestion)
blurb: Public French-language conference closing the 40th-anniversary series of the Valais computer-science school: Prof. Sébastien Gard on how SAP, Odoo and other ERP systems connect business functions and are changing with cloud and AI, plus braintec CEO Philipp Fux on digital transformation, followed by an apéritif.

title: dbt Meetup Zurich
blurb: Evening for the Zürich dbt community aimed at analytics engineers, data engineers and data leaders, opening with Massimo Turola of Bank Vontobel on using dbt to manage Snowflake Cortex AI applications in an AI data catalog, then an apéro.

title: Business mit KI. Heute, nicht 2030. Vol. 02 — Führung ist kein Prompt
blurb: Second volume of the Lucerne series for entrepreneurs and C-level leaders on how AI reshapes teams, leadership and the job market: two short talks, a moderated panel and an apéro, capped at 50 guests and held in German.

title: Workplace & Security Ninja User Group Switzerland 2612
organiser: Workplace & Security Ninja User Group Switzerland
blurb: Full day of community sessions on Microsoft endpoint, identity and security work, including securing agent identities, privileged-access strategy with Entra and Intune, secure low-code on the Power Platform, and label engineering.

title: AI Made in Europe: Built Here. Scaled Everywhere.
organiser: The Founder's Story, a Google Cloud series
blurb: The season finale of Google Cloud's Founder's Story series: a panel on whether Europe can build its own global AI companies or will mostly buy AI from elsewhere, covering research, open models, compute, sovereignty and capital, followed by a networking apéro at Google's Europaallee office.

title: Geneva 3D — Building a Living 3D Model of a Canton with AI Agents and Open Data
venue: Tesla showroom, Rue de la Confédération 8
organiser: Switzerland AI Community with Romandy CTO, hosted by Tesla
blurb: Arnaud Ricci on how he built Genève 3D, a browser-based 3D model of the whole canton, using AI agents and open data — with a live demonstration, questions from the room and a non-alcoholic apéro. The talk is in French with English subtitles.

title: IA : puissance ou prudence ?
organiser: Alp ICT, as part of the City of Geneva’s Semaine du climat 2026
blurb: A French-language citizen debate in Oxford style on the opportunities and risks of artificial intelligence: two teams coached by specialists argue before a jury of Geneva politicians, followed by an open discussion for SMEs and the public and an apéritif.

title: Hack Apertus — Onsite Hackathon Basel
blurb: The Basel leg of the national Apertus hackathon series, building applications and multilingual improvements on Switzerland’s open Apertus model at FHNW Campus Dreispitz, with everything produced released for reuse.

title: AI Society — AI Coffee Chats Zurich (4 December)
blurb: Fortnightly drop-in coffee hour for Zurich's AI practitioners: bring a question or a workflow to show, stay for as much of the hour as you like.

title: Christmas Special Hackathon — Operation Silent Night
blurb: Festive team hackathon where the Zurich Databricks User Group turns a sabotage mystery into hands-on practice with Genie, Lakebase and Databricks Apps.

title: Azure Zurich User Group X-Mas Special 2026
blurb: The Azure Zürich User Group closes the year with its Christmas get-together at Frau Gerolds Wintergarten — no agenda, just food, glühwein and the Swiss Azure community. Places are limited.

title: KubeVirt in Practice & AI in QA: What Works, What Doesn't
blurb: Two talks in Zurich: Red Hat's Simon Krenger on running virtual machines next to containers with KubeVirt, including live demos and when it is the wrong tool, and Basia Karaagac on where AI genuinely helps in QA and where exploratory testing and human risk judgement still win.

title: Fabric Year in Review 2026 — Highlights & Outlook
organiser: Data and AI for Intelligent Cloud
blurb: Year-end session from the Zurich Microsoft data-platform group on what actually shipped in Fabric during 2026 and what is worth planning for next.

title: AI-Stammtisch | Buchs
venue: OST Campus Buchs, Gebäude 1, Raum 1414 (CREALAB), Werdenbergstrasse 4
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (ICE Institut für Computational Engineering)
blurb: The Rhine valley edition of OST’s monthly AI round table: an informal evening in the Buchs CREALAB where university experts talk through how the technology actually works and how to point it at a problem you already have.

title: Robots, Agents and the Future of Work
venue: Université de Fribourg, Campus de Pérolles, PER 21, Boulevard de Pérolles 90
blurb: A panel with Peter Fankhauser (co-founder and CEO of ANYbotics) and Anne Scherer (co-founder of Delta Labs) on how AI is changing company operations, from autonomous robots on the plant floor to generative AI in the boardroom.

title: AI-Lunch Basel: Brown Bag
blurb: Deliberately low-key lunch break for Basel's AI crowd: no slides and no preparation, just an open exchange of learnings and use cases across industries.

title: The Night of Data Talents: Startup Edition
blurb: Swiss data startups pitch to an investor panel with community voting, capping the year for the Suisse Romande data scene.

title: Swiss Viz Awards 2026 — Award Ceremony
venue: HSLU Design Film Kunst, Project Space Building 745, Nylsuisseplatz 1
organiser: Swiss Viz Awards (Interactive Things) with Data Visualization Zurich
blurb: The Swiss Viz Awards ceremony at the Lucerne School of Design, Film and Art: a keynote from data-visualisation designer Moritz Stefaner, the awards themselves with entrants and jury in the room, then an apéro — joined by the Data Visualization Zurich community as a field trip.

title: AI Futures: Navigating the Future
venue: ETH Zurich Main Building, Rämistrasse 101, Room F 26.5
blurb: Closing session of the AI Futures series, moving from grand plans to personal ones: how people actually get into AI safety work, what to do about personal finances under uncertainty, and how to handle information overload and keep your footing.

title: AI-Powered SDLC: Zurich Tech Leaders Evening
blurb: Four practitioner talks for CTOs and engineering leaders on AI in software delivery: a year of lessons from building with AI, securing the software lifecycle against prompt injection and compromised agents, making enterprise data ready for AI agents, and AI-assisted delivery inside regulated healthcare.

title: From Parallel Token Prediction to Scalable Language Models
venue: ETH AI Center Foyer, OAT X 11, Andreasstrasse 5, Oerlikon
blurb: Prof. Stephan Mandt (UC Irvine) on generating several mutually consistent tokens in one forward pass — models pretrained to 3 billion parameters that approach autoregressive quality with inference up to 5.7× faster. Hosted by Prof. Julia Vogt.

title: AI for Business: Network, Learn & Grow in Zurich
venue: ibis Styles Zurich City Center, Stampfenbachstrasse 60
cost: Ticket required via Eventfrog (some early-bird tickets free; drinks not included)
blurb: December edition of the small-room series where founders and executives compare how they actually use AI: an invited talk, group conversations on what worked and what failed, then open networking.

title: Davos Catalyst: AI Summit 2027
venue: Davos Event Lounge, Rätia Center, Promenade 40
cost: CHF 7,900 delegate pass (CHF 5,900 until 31 October, excl. VAT)
blurb: Invitation-only summit running alongside Davos week for around 200 founders, investors, corporate leaders and researchers, with roundtables and closed-door sessions on AI infrastructure, investment, enterprise deployment and governance.

title: Software Engineering in der Vibe-Code-Ära
venue: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule, Campus Rapperswil, Raum 1.213
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (Institut für Computational Engineering)
cost: CHF 600 (materials, refreshments and a follow-up online clinic included)
blurb: One-day German-language course for senior engineers, tech leads and CTOs who already code with agentic tools: build your own eval suite, an MCP tool wired to your build and test commands, a CI hook that blocks bad AI patches, and a cost-per-feature model comparison — working on your own repository. Limited to 16 participants.

title: AI House Davos 2027
blurb: Five days of AI programming on the Davos Promenade alongside the World Economic Forum, bringing research, industry, policy and civil society together under the 2027 theme "Citizens of an expanding world".

title: digitalswitzerland @ Davos
blurb: A full day in Davos on Switzerland's digital future, with speakers from business, government and research building on the national AI Action Plan and looking ahead to the Geneva AI Summit 2027. Programme details still to be published.

title: AI-Stammtisch Basel: Input und Diskussion am Abend
venue: iRIX Software Engineering AG, Gundeldinger Feld, Bau 5, Dornacherstrasse 192
blurb: The Basel AI Stammtisch returns for the new year with a guest talk or an in-house topic, followed by open discussion over drinks at the iRIX bistro.

title: Digital Lounge @ Davos — Enterprise Data, AI & Robotics
blurb: An invitation-only forum during Davos week for CxOs and transformation leaders on enterprise data, AI and robotics — morning and afternoon keynotes and panels, a live technology showcase, entrepreneur talks and parallel workshops, closing with an awards ceremony and dinner.

title: Generative AI for Epidemiology Researchers: Practical Skills and Responsible Use
blurb: A three-day course in Wengen on using generative AI responsibly in research, pairing lectures with computer practicals on analysis, literature searching, scientific writing, study websites and agentic AI — and on where error, bias and reproducibility break down.

title: AI for Decision Makers — Executive Course at ETH Zurich
time: 09:00–17:00 on 22, 28 and 29 January and 4 and 5 February
organiser: Swiss Data Science Center / ETH Zürich School for Continuing Education
cost: CHF 4,000 (10% off for ETH staff and alumni and SDSC partners)
blurb: A five-day English-language executive course for leaders who need to challenge assumptions on AI projects without becoming data scientists — data science foundations, MLOps, AI governance and ethics, generative AI and a first agent, with an ETH Zurich certificate. Registration closes 15 January 2027.

title: Generative AI & Agentische Systeme
organiser: OST – Ostschweizer Fachhochschule (Institut für Computational Engineering)
blurb: Two-day German-language course for developers, architects, data scientists and ML engineers on building agentic LLM systems that survive production: function calling, hybrid-search RAG, LangGraph topologies, security hardening and systematic evaluation. Places are limited.

title: SWAT4HCLS 2027
blurb: The 15th edition of the long-running international conference on semantics in healthcare and life sciences — ontologies, knowledge graphs and AI — with keynotes, tutorials and a dedicated biohackathon day in Basel.

title: SDSC-Connect: Connecting Digital Environmental Sciences
venue: Central Bern venue to be announced
blurb: A day in Bern on making environmental data usable across disciplines and institutions — data access and sharing, data infrastructure, and the role of machine learning and AI across climate, ecology, hydrology, the cryosphere, natural hazards and agriculture, with keynotes, invited talks, break-outs and a poster fair. Seats are limited and the venue is still to be announced.

title: AI & Quantum Course: From Foundations to Scalable Intelligence
blurb: An afternoon course run with Quantum Basel, led by its CTO Jan Mikolon, bridging current AI practice and quantum technologies — from the foundations through to what it takes to scale.

title: Hack Apertus — Midway
venue: Novu Campus @ The Circle, The Circle 60
blurb: The mid-series afternoon of the national Hack Apertus initiative: Imanol Schlag (ETH), Thomas Taroni (Phoeniqs) and David Gugelmann (Exeon Analytics) on the model, the infrastructure and the security, three hackathon projects showing what they built, then parallel Q&A tables and a closing reception.

title: Kickstart AI Workflows with Databricks
organiser: Swiss Data & AI Group (Databricks User Group)
blurb: Hybrid Databricks user-group evening in Zurich on automating data work with AI-enabled workflows, including a session on Databricks Apps and Lakebase applied to clinical cancer research cohorts. Rescheduled from November 2026 to February 2027.

title: AI Days 2027 — Geneva
blurb: Geneva leg of the fifth AI Days, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, with workshops, talks, research and demos. Registration not yet open.

title: AI Days 2027 — Yverdon-les-Bains
blurb: Yverdon-les-Bains leg of AI Days 2027, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, with workshops, talks and demos. Registration not yet open.

title: AI Days 2027 — Fribourg
blurb: Fribourg leg of AI Days 2027, the Swiss AI Center’s applied-AI conference for SMEs, closing the three-city edition with workshops, talks and demos. Registration not yet open.

title: GenAI Zürich 2027
blurb: A two-day European summit on applied generative AI at the Volkshaus: keynotes, panels, workshops, roundtables, a hackathon, startup pitches and the GenAI Zürich Award, focused on what works in production.

title: IMD KI-Update 2027
organiser: echo originals AG (with IMD as knowledge partner)
cost: CHF 890 (early bird CHF 712 until 15 November 2026; CHF 623 per person for teams of five or more)
blurb: A one-day German-language management congress on leading in the AI era: executive cases, keynotes on efficiency, growth, trust and responsibility, and a closing keynote by Richard David Precht.

title: Swiss Legal Tech Conference 2027
blurb: A day of sessions on legal technology and AI in practice: comprehensive data management and whether data lakes break down silos, risk and exit management for legal tech, courts in the age of AI, and what role AI agents play today.
